summary: On-demand redacted per-tenant webhook for SIEM (Azure Sentinel) + completed SIGv2 answers and sample connector
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Finarc Bank, enterprise) requests a turnkey deliverable combining two items: 1) an on-demand, per-tenant webhook export to Azure Sentinel that delivers tamper-evident envelope events with field-level pseudonymization/redaction based on consent flags; and 2) completed SIGv2 questionnaire answers and a short sample connector (ARM template + Function) demonstrating HMAC verification and X509 pinning.

Impact:
- Customer cannot complete their SOC attestation until they receive a SIEM integration example and SIGv2 evidence.
- Compliance team needs proof of redaction logic and tamper-evidence for PII-heavy audit entries.

Environment:
- Customer production tenants in us-east (primary) and eu-west (secondary).
- Tenant-level audit stream currently enabled, delivered as our per-tenant webhook with JSON v2 envelope.

Request details / Acceptance criteria:
1) Sample Azure Sentinel connector (ARM + Azure Function) that ingests our webhook, validates HMAC signature, verifies X509 chain, and writes events to Sentinel workspace.
2) Example envelope with demonstrated field-level pseudonymization rules (email, user_id, prompt_text) plus a mode showing redaction vs pseudonymization for legal hold cases.
3) Tamper-evidence: include a transparent checksum/hmac and an example of signed checkpoint manifest for hourly batches.
4) SIGv2 questionnaire: PDQ-complete answers for the audit/export-related controls and a short list of evidentiary artifacts we can deliver (logs, export-manifests, KMS key rotation proof).
5) Minimal code sample (Python) and a short runbook for the customer's security team describing how to validate proofs and troubleshoot failures.

Steps to reproduce (how customer configured):
1) Enabled tenant audit streaming in Console for tenant finarc-prod-us.
2) Set delivery target to webhook endpoint but left signature verification off initially while testing.
3) Requested evidence bundle and SIGv2 answers via account rep on 2026-03-09.

Logs / Sample payloads attached in comments below.
steps_to_reproduce: See description for customer configuration steps; customer can switch to 'deliver on-demand' from Console -> Audit -> On-demand exports
comments: 2026-03-11 09:14 - Maya Chen (Customer): Initial request and questionnaire attached. Customer stressed timeline: security review scheduled 2026-03-20.
2026-03-11 11:02 - Aisha Patel (Support): Acknowledged. Assigning SRE and Security Eng to produce connector example and SIGv2 answers. Creating internal sandbox tenant for testing.
2026-03-12 15:35 - Carlos Rivera (Security Eng): Requested clarification on acceptable pseudonymization algorithms (salt vs keyed HMAC). Asked for customer's legal preference.

2026-03-13 10:28 - Finarc Security Contact (customer): Prefers reversible pseudonymization for legal hold (deterministic HMAC with KMS-wrapped key), redaction for default exports. Allowed us-east storage only.

2026-03-14 08:50 - Aisha Patel (Support): Drafted SIGv2 answers (attached) and initial connector prototype uploaded to PR. Marking as In Progress for SRE to harden HMAC verification and manifest signing.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 - SRE (Aisha): Verified current audit-exporter can emit an 'on-demand' zipped manifest of last-hour events. Payloads include tenant_id and event_type. No deterministic pseudonymization option currently in prod exporters; we have 'redact' mode only.

2026-03-12 - Security Eng (Carlos): Feasibility check: deterministic HMAC pseudonymization can be implemented as a post-export transform using KMS-wrapped key; requires minor exporter change to accept tenancy-specific key_id. Risk: introduces key management surface and rotation complexity.

2026-03-13 - Dev (Rina Gupta): Built prototype transform in sandbox that applies HMAC-SHA256(email, tenant_key) and emits envelope_signature hmac over canonicalized payload. Performance: extra CPU ~8% for peak export loads in sandbox tests.
workarounds: Provided temporary guidance to customer: 1) Use redaction mode for now (available) and request signed batch manifests for non-repudiation. 2) Use our provided ARM + Function sample in read-only mode (signature verification disabled) to demonstrate ingestion while we finalize HMAC flow.
next_steps: 1) SRE to implement tenant-key parameter and deterministic pseudonymization in exporter (ETA 2026-03-20). 2) Security to finalize SIGv2 answers and attach evidentiary artifacts (logs, signed manifests, KMS rotation policy) by 2026-03-16. 3) Deliver final connector and runbook to Finarc and schedule verification call.
resolution_notes: In Progress - no resolution yet. Draft SIGv2 answers are attached and connector prototype exists. Waiting on SRE PR to add deterministic pseudonymization support and KMS key binding.
external_communications: We have proposed a 30-min technical review with Finarc on 2026-03-17. Account rep assigned: Jordan Hayes.
